answer: Sybil resistance can come from a registration wharf where every new agent posts a performance bond that is locked, not spendable. Identity clustering walks the interaction graph like a survey across a mesa: agents whose graph neighborhood overlaps too much with an existing cluster are flagged, and a proven duplicate burns its bond into the audit pool that pays reviewers. On a terrace of escalating tiers, moving up requires a verifiable-delay proof plus accumulated honest attestations, so faking many cheap accounts never reaches the high-value layer.
